messages:
Olivia Chen: Hey team — BrightApps reached out asking for a post-incident summary + timeline for the degradation last night. They want: RCA summary, exact affected window, #requests/users impacted, mitigation we did, and what we're doing to prevent recurrence. Planning to send a formal note to their security and ops leads by EOD PST. Can SRE confirm numbers + a concise root cause? cc @Tariq (oncall)

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-14T22:10:24Z created (sev=P2) — paging oncall @Tariq Malik. Service: redwood-generation-us-west, symptom: increased 5xx rate and sustained tail latency >5s for streaming responses. Auto-fallback triggered to model-variant v2-quant-fallback at 22:25 UTC.

Tariq Malik: 1) quick summary from oncall: we started getting alerts ~22:09 UTC for elevated 5xx and queue growth. 2) immediate mitigation: rolled traffic away from the new model variant (v2.3.1) to previous stable (v2.2.9) at 22:18 UTC, scaled dedicated pool by +2 machines at 22:21 UTC, restarted stuck worker processes on shard-7 at 22:26 UTC. Positive effect seen ~22:32 UTC.

Sam Park: RCA (concise): root cause was a memory leak in the KV-cache eviction path in the serving runtime introduced by the streaming cache refactor in v2.3.1. Under certain long-sequence streaming workloads the eviction task could requeue itself repeatedly and exhaust local memory, leading to OOMs and worker crashes which produced 5xx. The bug only surfaced under sustained long-sequence traffic and the new quantized kernels' scheduling pattern exacerbated the timing.

Sam Park: Timeline (for the customer note):
- 22:08 UTC — first error-rate spike observed by synthetic checks.
- 22:10 UTC — incident auto-detected; page sent to oncall.
- 22:15 UTC — engineering triage, identified correlation with v2.3.1 rollout and streaming-enabled requests.
- 22:18 UTC — traffic routing change: shift to v2.2.9 for affected routes.
- 22:21 UTC — scaled dedicated pool + enabled emergency burst capacity.
- 22:26 UTC — restarted worker processes on shard-7 (cleared OOM loops).
- 22:32 UTC — metrics show recovery trend; 5xx rate back to baseline by 22:42 UTC.

Marta Ruiz: Customer impact (BrightApps): their routed requests hit the affected cluster between 22:12–22:30 UTC. We saw ~12 failing requests and 237 unique end-users affected (based on request IDs in our logs). Latency degradation observed up to ~8s for streaming responses before rollback. I can export the specific request IDs to attach to the customer if they ask.

Olivia Chen: Drafting the customer message — putting a proposed template here for quick edits: 
```
Hi <BrightApps Ops>,
Thanks for flagging this. We had a service degradation impacting streaming responses on redwood-generation-us-west on 2026-03-14 between 22:08–22:42 UTC. Root cause: a memory leak triggered in the KV-cache eviction path introduced in a recent runtime change paired with streaming long-sequence requests. Impact: 12 failed requests and ~237 end-users affected; tail latency for some requests reached ~8s.
Mitigation: we rolled traffic back to the previous model variant, scaled the dedicated pool, and restarted affected workers — service returned to baseline by 22:42 UTC.
Preventative actions: a hotfix to the eviction task has been merged to staging, automated regression test for streaming long-sequences added, and we will delay further v2.3.x rollouts until we complete a canary run with additional telemetry.
We propose a 5% credit on March usage for the BrightApps accounts that hit errors while we investigate — please let us know if you'd prefer alternate remediation.
Thanks,
Olivia on behalf of Redwood Inference
```

Olivia Chen: Note: legal sign-off required on the credit language. tagging @Legal Bot for approval.

Legal Bot: Suggested edit — replace "We propose a 5% credit" with "We are offering a one-time account credit equivalent to 5% of billed usage for impacted requests in March 2026. This is a goodwill accommodation and not an admission of liability." Approved by legal for CS to send.

Sam Park: Hotfix status: PR #12345 implementing a guarded eviction loop and an additional memory quota check has passed CI and is on the canary environment. Plan: push to dedicated pools tomorrow 02:00 UTC with a short canary (30m) and extended telemetry. Owner: Sam Park.

Sam Park: Longer-term fixes + mitigations:
- Add per-worker eviction task circuit-breaker (done in PR #12345).
- Add synthetic canary that exercises long-sequence streaming RPCs to catch regressions. Owner: Eng-ML. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Improve observability: new metric for eviction-loop-requeues + alert when requeues > 100/min. Owner: Eng-Infra. ETA: 1 week.

Marta Ruiz: Customer ops ask: should we include raw request IDs in the email or attach them in a secure support ticket? BrightApps tends to prefer an attachment. I can prepare a CSV and attach it under the support portal.

Olivia Chen: Let's attach CSV via support portal (safer). Marta, can you produce the file and drop a link? Also I'll send the draft to BrightApps' security and ops leads once legal confirms the credit wording. Target send: today 17:00 PST.

Tariq Malik: Post-incident oncall notes: I filed an action item in the oncall board to run a one-off sweep for similar requeues across all clusters, and bumped the rate limit for model rollout concurrency in our config to reduce blast radius by default.

Olivia Chen: OK — actions summary for the customer note (so they get a clear list):
- Brief RCA summary (one paragraph) — Sam
- Exact impacted window and counts — Marta
- Mitigations performed — Tariq
- Preventative actions & timeline — Sam
- Credit language (legal-approved) — Olivia
I'll assemble and circulate for a quick +1. If nobody raises objections I'll send at 17:00 PST.

Sam Park: +1 on technical wording.

Marta Ruiz: +1 on counts and CSV ready, uploading to support portal now: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/BRIGHT-542/attachment/impact-ids.csv

Olivia Chen: Thanks all — I'll post the status page update draft alongside the customer email and mark this thread as follow-up when sent.

Olivia Chen: (follow-up at 17:12 PST) Sent to BrightApps ops+security: https://support.redwood.ai/threads/BRIGHT-542 (copy of message attached). Will update here if they reply or request changes.
